workflow.remark: The full 3-degree cone cannot be loaded: it holds 255,553 Gaia DR3 sources (count on 2026-10-13), and the anonymous Gaia archive returns at most 50,000 rows. Load a pre-filtered extract with one ADQL query and give the exact command in the table entry: e2er-data gaia query --adql "SELECT source_id, ra, dec, DISTANCE(POINT('ICRS', ra, dec), POINT('ICRS', 56.75, 24.12)) AS dist_deg, parallax, parallax_error, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmra_error, pmdec, pmdec_error, ruwe, astrometric_params_solved, visibility_periods_used, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_g_mean_flux_over_error, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1 = CONTAINS(POINT('ICRS', ra, dec), CIRCLE('ICRS', 56.75, 24.12, 3)) AND parallax > 2 AND parallax_over_error > 5" --table gaia_dr3 --save-to gaia_dr3.csv. This returned 14,066 rows on 2026-10-13. Say in the dictionary that the extract keeps parallax above 2 mas (closer than 500 pc) and parallax_over_error above 5, so the field background in the CMD is limited to these stars, and that every cut of the sensitivity grid lies inside this extract. Also fix the description of astrometric_params_solved: 3 = two-parameter (position only), 31 = five-parameter, 95 = six-parameter solution.

workflow.text: Researcher decisions at the design review: the plan's 'pull the full cone, not a pre-filtered subset' is replaced by the pre-filtered extract (parallax > 2 mas, parallax_over_error > 5) because the archive's anonymous limit is 50,000 rows and the cone holds 255,553 sources; the paper says so. The grid row 'parallax_over_error > 5' is therefore the loosest quality cut available. workflow.remark: Two corrections. (1) sigma/sqrt(n) is the standard error of the mean, not of the median (for a normal distribution the median's is about 1.25 times larger). In the design section and in the parallax results, call the 0.007 mas value the standard error of the mean parallax, and drop the sentence that the median is determined far more precisely than its scatter would suggest. (2) The brightest member has G = 5.20, so the cluster's brightest stars (the named B stars, several magnitudes brighter) are not among the members. State this in the CMD results and the limitations as a gap at the bright end, without guessing which cut removed them. Change nothing else.
